players.product: NdPr oxide and sintered NdFeB permanent magnets

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: the company generated $126.1 million of revenue and PPA income, more than doubling last year's revenue, driven primarily by the 127% increase in NdPr sales volumes; consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $28.5 million, a $41 million improvement year-over-year; adjusted diluted EPS improved $0.12 to a loss of $0.01 per share.
quarterly_data.figure: $126.1 million revenue and PPA income; adjusted EBITDA $28.5 million (+$41 million YoY); adjusted diluted EPS loss of $0.01

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the Materials segment generated $113.2 million of revenue plus PPA income and $32.5 million of adjusted EBITDA, a $45 million year-over-year improvement. CFO: sequentially, Materials revenue plus PPA income was essentially flat (identical sales volumes, impact of the price floor); Magnetics revenue declined slightly as a much higher proportion of costs went to the start-up of magnet production versus precursor products; consolidated adjusted EBITDA declined modestly on the planned biannual Mountain Pass shutdown and the Magnetics transition ahead of commercial magnet revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Materials: $113.2 million revenue plus PPA income; $32.5 million adjusted EBITDA (+$45 million YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Materials produced 840 metric tons of NdPr, up 41% year-over-year and consistent with expectations, despite an extended planned plant shutdown in April. COO: the scheduled semi-annual maintenance outage, extended by unrelated projects and pilot testing, affected the quarter; mid-stream shows significant year-over-year growth and steady sequential improvement, with a handful of circuits still presenting reliability challenges affecting yield and throughput being addressed through equipment upgrades and process enhancements.
quarterly_data.figure: 840 metric tons NdPr produced; up 41% year-over-year

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: customer demand continues to outpace production growth; NdPr sales exceeded 1,000 metric tons for the second consecutive quarter, up 127% year-over-year. CFO: demand for NdPr remains extremely strong; as of June 30 approximately 650 metric tons of NdPr oxide and metal were on hand, in transit, at toll processors or waiting for shipment.
quarterly_data.figure: NdPr sales exceeded 1,000 metric tons (+127% YoY); approximately 650 metric tons NdPr oxide and metal on hand as of June 30

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 outlook. COO: based on current performance, expects Q3 NdPr production to exceed 1,000 metric tons (CEO: significant volume growth next quarter toward the targeted year-end NdPr production run rate). CFO: realized NdPr oxide pricing expected in the high $90s per kilogram, leaving PPA income at roughly $10 per kilogram; with market pricing about $110 per kilogram early in Q3, minimal PPA income expected from stockpiled NdPr in concentrate, so a slight sequential decline in overall PPA income; Materials sales volumes expected flattish, depending on sales mix, shipment timing and metallization lead times. CFO: full-year CapEx still expected in the $500 million to $600 million range.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 NdPr production to exceed 1,000 metric tons; realized NdPr oxide price high $90s per kilogram; PPA income roughly $10 per kilogram; full-year CapEx $500 million to $600 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: in July MP entered into a long-term agreement to supply gadolinium oxide to a leading U.S. aerospace and defense manufacturer (not named), expected to be a sizable nine-figure deal in total over multiple years that expands the heavy rare earth product portfolio at attractive returns. CFO: economics are locked in (no spot price exposure); opportunity to grow volumes over time at significant incremental return; the gadolinium comes from the SEG product left after separating dysprosium and terbium. COO: after a successful extended pilot campaign, moving forward with engineering and procurement to complete the gadolinium separation project on a similar time line to samarium.

Customer General Motors: during the quarter MP delivered magnets to GM for in-vehicle qualification testing; commercial magnet shipments from Independence expected to begin in the fourth quarter with modest volumes, followed by a steady production ramp. COO: substantial progress in GM qualification while scaling toward 24/7 production across all major processes; now demonstrating the capability and consistency required to support customers' volume ramp. CFO: qualification covers capacity staging per motor plant, batch traceability and quality-system integration and vehicle-level part-swap impact; results extremely encouraging.
quarterly_data.figure: commercial magnet shipments expected to begin in Q4

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Independence is fully sold out between GM and Apple, and it is possible another customer or two fits in; 10X is 100% contracted with the Department of Defense, and as the facility comes online MP will likely end up contracting almost all of that capacity to industry rather than to the Department of Defense. CEO: 'we have everything fully contracted if that's what we want'; strong interest from customers across automotive, industrial, aerospace, defense and emerging physical AI applications; expects additional customer announcements over time. CFO: customer engagement extremely high, but no rush to announce deals.
quarterly_data.figure: Independence fully sold out; 10X 100% contracted with the Department of Defense

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: precursor production generated adjusted EBITDA margins exceeding 40%. CFO: approximately $46 million of prepaid revenue remains to be earned for magnetic precursor products over the next three to four quarters on a modestly declining basis; after that MP will no longer produce these products for external sale and will dedicate metal production capacity to finished magnets. CFO: in Q2 MP began operating commercial magnet production facilities for trial shipments and run-rate testing, with overhead, labor and materials costs not yet inventoriable; behind the scenes it had its best metal production quarter ever; the precursor-to-magnet transition will be lumpy and nonlinear, with more on the 2027 cadence near year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: precursor adjusted EBITDA margins exceeding 40%; approximately $46 million prepaid revenue remaining

quarterly_data.signal: COO: the partnership with Apple on magnet recycling, magnet production and joint development continues to advance; recycling's primary focus is process waste from Independence and 10X in supporting Apple, with scaling in line with market conditions. CFO: current efforts support scaled production for GM and the follow-on contracts with Apple and the Department of Defense.

CFO: Q2 CapEx was $230.3 million, a little over 60% attributable to the Magnetics segment, including the approximately $80 million acquisition of the 10X site; year-to-date spend $308 million as of June 30. CFO: $1.45 billion of cash and short-term investments at quarter end, which with improving operating cash flow fully funds the long-term capital plan.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 CapEx $230.3 million; 10X site approximately $80 million; YTD $308 million; $1.45 billion cash and short-term investments

quarterly_data.signal: 10X magnet facility: CEO: foundation work is underway, long lead production equipment has been ordered, and at the close of the call the site was 'officially vertical'. COO: Independence learnings and customer feedback are being built into final equipment selection and detailed engineering; the project is advancing to plan and very much on track.

Heavy rare earths. COO: mechanical completion of the first heavy rare earth separation circuit in May; feed to be introduced imminently; on track to produce terbium and dysprosium later this year (CEO: shipping product from Mountain Pass to Independence later this year). COO: samarium program engineering and procurement advancing, first production planned in 2028 (CFO: committed in the Department of Defense agreements). COO: the circuit can process third-party feedstocks and is designed for a mix of samarium, gadolinium, terbium, yttrium; CFO: MP will be producing a yttrium product. CFO: Dy/Tb output goes into inventory and is recognized through magnet sales.

Mountain Pass projects (COO): breaking ground this month on an expanded area to house magnet recycling plus additional heavy rare earth separation and finishing; chlor-alkali recommissioning advanced with additional brine pre-treatment online and early positive crystallizer results; a full-plant reagent trial led to a planned reagent change later this year at a modestly higher direct cost (COO confirmed the new reagent is not from China); a new pre-flot process is expected at scale by 2028; early exploratory drilling suggests potential additional ore within the existing pit contours.

CFO on costs: the path to a lower cost structure is very clear, via consistent operation at target production levels (fixed-cost absorption), process efficiency, lower maintenance intensity and chlor-alkali; benefits expected to build progressively through '27. CFO on the China export ban: expects minimal impact and no immediate impact, as the supply chain has been prepared to be resilient.

CEO: 'NdPr is the binding constraint' in magnets for the foreseeable future; the world is in a regime of 'controlled scarcity' with no or very limited heavy rare earths leaving China and magnets on a licensing basis, causing real disruption from allocations in the industrial supply chain, particularly aerospace. CEO: if the world produced 30 million or 40 million humanoid robots a year, that alone would consume 100% of global rare earth magnet production, including China.
quarterly_data.figure: 30 million or 40 million humanoid robots a year would consume 100% of global rare earth magnet production (CEO)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Project Swarm, launched with U.S. and allied drone manufacturers to aggregate and standardize future magnet demand around the Department of Defense preferred grades to be produced at 10X; subscription agreements already signed with a number of participants. CEO: drone production may be around 12 million a year, which MP estimates might be somewhere between 500 and 1,000 tons of magnet demand, essentially 100% in China today; demand is immaterial today (the entire American drone industry is smaller than MP's GM business) but could be quite large three to five years out.
quarterly_data.figure: drone magnet demand estimated between 500 and 1,000 tons (CEO estimate)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: MP has made remarkable strides reducing heavy rare earths needed; the vast majority of demand (e.g. robotics, disk drives) is no-heavy, and by the time 10X comes online the vast majority of the facility will require no or very limited heavies. COO: heavy rare earth intensity is being reduced through Grain Boundary Diffusion and other process innovations; products meet and exceed customer specifications for magnetic, temperature and corrosion performance; a team of 100-plus engineers develops magnet design, chemistry and micro-structure.

CEO view: AI is approaching a transition from creating intelligence to deploying it into the physical economy (machines that manufacture, move, build, transport and defend); MP sees this as a structural, not cyclical, shift that makes resilient domestic production of critical materials and components increasingly important over the coming decade; robotics use cases depend more on size, weight and torque density, making magnet substitution harder.
